label: pjm 33 miso reanchor
definition: Forecast-grade reference-price interchange seam (pjm_32 lineage) with the dominant MISO seam now anchored entirely to MISO's OWN measured Indiana-Hub RT LMP (fetched from docs.misoenergy.org), replacing estimates (claude.md #12): marginal heat rate 14.2->12.9 (14.2 used the IMM ~$36 all-footprint average; the border Indiana Hub measures $31.8/$30.8/$42.85 = LMP/HH 12.5/14.1/12.2, mean 12.9 -> 14.2 over-priced the border by +13%/+17% in 2023/2025) and convexity 1.63->1.60 (self-derived, R2 0.24 -- confirms the borrow was sound, so convexity was NOT the over-export driver; the level was). derive_neighbor_convexity --check now guards both. RESULT vs pjm_32: net export corrects toward measured every year -- 2024 +34%->+1.8% (33.3 vs 32.7 TWh, near-perfect), 2025 +112%->+30% (23.4 vs 18.0), 2023 +56%->+32% (52.7 vs 40.0); in-tol fails 7->5; 2024 now fully passes (coal-tot +1.0%, gas +4.8%). HONEST TRADE-OFF: with interchange correctly sized the LMP under-run is no longer masked by over-export -- 2025 LMP -13.7% (was pjm_32 -10.5%, pjm_28 -16.8%), 2024 -6.4%, 2023 +2.1% -- revealing the residual under-run is PJM's OWN price-formation gap (scarcity/congestion/reserve adders the energy-only LP omits), NOT interchange. Residual coal-over in 2023/2025 (+7%) is the forecast-native single MISO HR (12.9) slightly over-pricing those years (their measured ratios 12.5/12.2 < 12.9); a per-year HR would close it but isn't forecastable. Most structurally faithful PJM run to date (every seam parameter measured from the neighbor's own data, nothing tuned to PJM flow, rule #11); pjm_28 remains the lowest-fail FITTED reference.
